draft.title: Volume of rectangular prisms
card: Volume is the amount of space inside a 3D object. We measure it in cubic units, such as cubic centimetres (\(\text{cm}^{3}\)) or cubic metres (\(\text{m}^{3}\)).
A rectangular prism is a box shape. Its volume is \(V = l \times w \times h\), where \(l\) is length, \(w\) is width and \(h\) is height.
Worked example: a box is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high. \(V = 5 \times 3 \times 2 = 30\), so the volume is \(30 \text{ cm}^{3}\).
All three lengths must be in the same unit before you multiply. The answer is then in that unit cubed. Area uses squared units such as \(\text{cm}^{2}\).
draft.remember: Multiply the three lengths. The answer is in cubic units.

a.q: A fish tank is 40 cm long, 20 cm wide and 25 cm high. What is its volume?
a.why: \(V = 40 \times 20 \times 25 = 20{,}000\), and volume is in cubic units, so \(\text{cm}^{3}\). Adding the lengths gives 85, which is not how volume works. Using \(\text{cm}^{2}\) is tempting, but that is a unit for area.
a.clue: Multiply all three lengths, and use a cubic unit.

b.q: Priya's storage box is 2 m long, 50 cm wide and 40 cm high. What is its volume in cubic centimetres?
b.why: Change 2 m to 200 cm first. Then \(V = 200 \times 50 \times 40 = 400{,}000\), so the volume is \(400{,}000 \text{ cm}^{3}\). Using 2 instead of 200 gives 4,000, which mixes units.
b.clue: Put every length in centimetres before multiplying.
